Read sqlglot parser in the installed venv (/Users/the01geek/repos/sqllens/.venv, pyproject pins sqlglot>=25.0,<31; I could not execute code, so this is by reading one installed version only, not every version in the range). _parse_table: the fast path (_parse_table_parts_fast, parser.py:5030-5047) retreats and returns None when an identifier is followed by L_PAREN (TABLE_POSTFIX_TOKENS, parser.py:912-914), so a function call falls to the slow path. _parse_table_parts (5093-5140) calls _parse_table_part (5022-5028), which first tries _parse_function(optional_parens=False). _parse_function_call (7523-7638) turns `name(` with a non-known name into exp.Anonymous(this=<written text, case preserved>, expressions=args) (7627), so pragma_table_info('t') and PRAGMA_Index_List('t') yield exp.Table(this=exp.Anonymous) with the written name. Dialect-independent code, so it holds for sqlite and no dialect. A bare pragma_table_list has no following L_PAREN, so _parse_function_call returns None (7551-7556); _parse_id_var then gives an Identifier, giving Table(this=Identifier) whose Table.name is the identifier text. readonly.py:204-206 handles both: Anonymous uses source.name, else table.name, then lowercases and checks the prefix. The claim matches.

readonly.py:195-197 checks isinstance(parsed, exp.Show) or (exp.Command and parsed.name.upper()=="SHOW"). In installed sqlglot: base Tokenizer.COMMANDS includes TokenType.SHOW (tokens.py:544-548), so _parse_statement (parser.py:2460-2461) calls _parse_command, which builds exp.Command(this=self._prev.text.upper()) = 'SHOW' (parser.py:2351-2357). MySQL removes SHOW from COMMANDS (dialects/mysql.py:171) and maps TokenType.SHOW to _parse_show (parsers/mysql.py:186); with no matching SHOW_PARSERS entry _parse_show falls to _parse_as_command(self._prev) (parser.py:9978-9982), which stores this=text[:len(start.text)] = the SHOW token text (case preserved; check applies .upper()) (parser.py:10060-10066). The start token is SHOW itself, so an inline comment after it (SHOW/**/TABLES) does not alter the stored name. Expression.name returns text of `this`, so the root name is 'SHOW'. Caveat: the parenthetical 'every non-MySQL dialect' is loose, since DuckDB, Snowflake and SingleStore define SHOW_PARSERS and yield exp.Show, but that case is covered by the isinstance(exp.Show) branch, and the shipped dialects (sqlite, postgres, mysql, None) match the claim. The rejections lines address other subjects (_format.py) and do not bear on this.

The only text change the guard makes before sqlglot.parse is _mysql_parse_sql (readonly.py:461-518, called at 536-538), which replaces '' with ' ' only inside '#'/'--' line comments. MySQL case: sqlglot MySQL Tokenizer sets COMMENTS_TERMINATE_AT_NEWLINE_ONLY = True (sqlglot/dialects/mysql.py:94) and the scan loop (tokenizer_core.py:932-941) then ends a line comment only at '
', so a '' inside a comment is comment text in the raw parse exactly as the space is in the rewritten one: same tokens, so the raw text parses at parse_one (readonly.py:168). No-dialect case: default tokenizer ends a comment at '' too (tokens.py:212-213), but the guard raises UnsafeSqlError for a bare '' in a line comment when no dialect (readonly.py:510-513), so an accepted query has only '
' endings; raw parse ends the comment at '' and treats '
' as whitespace, same token stream as the rewritten text. Postgres/sqlite are not rewritten at all (536). Unknown dialects become None in the classifier (157-164), matching no-dialect. Should parsing still fail, 169-176 returns False (result shown), as claimed. I read the code and the sqlglot tokenizer but did not execute a query. The rejections lines concern unknown dialects and components_to_markdown and do not affect this claim.

readonly.py:199-207 walks parsed.find_all(exp.Table), so a catalog table in a CTE, WHERE subquery or UNION branch is covered. It lowercases table.db and the name, so quoted mixed case is covered. It reads Anonymous table functions via table.this, so schema-qualified main.pragma_table_info('t') is covered when sqlglot parses it as a Table. The claim is absolute ('any catalog table', 'a table-valued function called in FROM'). I could not settle the LATERAL/JOIN-to-function input. sqlglot's _parse_lateral (sqlglot/parser.py:4735-4790) can set Lateral.this to a bare function (_parse_function) with no exp.Table node. A statement such as 'SELECT * FROM t, LATERAL pg_get_keywords() k' on postgres might then bypass the walk. Whether it does depends on whether _parse_select(table=True) consumes the name as a Table first, and I could not run sqlglot to check. No test in tests/ covers this (the only LATERAL hit is test_safety_rls.py:340). Missing evidence: the output of sqlglot.parse_one(..., dialect='postgres').find_all(exp.Table) for that statement. I did not run it.

The test (tests/unit/test_query_database.py:1137-1179) claims the configured dialect reaches the formatter. Its two catalog queries are 'SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()' and 'SELECT tablename FROM pg_catalog.pg_tables'. In src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py, is_introspection_query with dialect=None uses _catalog_names(None), which returns _ALL_CATALOG_SCHEMAS (information_schema, pg_catalog, mysql, sys, performance_schema) and all prefixes (readonly.py:102-105). The first query's table schema is information_schema and the second's is pg_catalog, both in that union. Both parse without a dialect, because DATABASE() is just an anonymous function. So both classify True with dialect=None, exactly as they do under mysql and postgres respectively. The test therefore passes even if query_database.py stopped passing the dialect, and it does not show what its docstring asserts. The rejections lines cover other findings (unknown dialect, components_to_markdown) and not this missing-discrimination test gap, so they do not apply.

Traced by reading sqlglot (repo .venv parser.py), not by running it. In 'SELECT FROM WHERE ;;;' FROM is followed by WHERE. WHERE is in TABLE_TERMINATORS (parser.py:1081) and is not an identifier token, so _parse_table_parts gets no table and reaches 'if not table and not is_db_reference: self.raise_error("Expected table name but got ...")' (parser.py:5135-5136). parse_one uses the default immediate error level, so this raises ParseError. The path is not dialect-specific, so it applies to mysql, postgres, sqlite and no dialect. is_introspection_query (src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:167-176) catches ParseError/TokenError and returns False (fail-open). The test at tests/unit/test_format.py:1936-1940 therefore exercises that fail-open path, and the table is shown. The first_sql_keyword check for SHOW does not match, because the first keyword is SELECT. Not executed, so confidence is high but not from a run.

readonly.py:116 sets line_markers = ('--', '#') only if dialect in (None, 'mysql'), else ('--',). Trace of '#x\nSHOW ...' with dialect='postgres' (the case the test comment sits on, test_safety.py:928-930): '#' is not stripped, so rest does not start with SHOW, so it is not a SHOW; for sqlite the same. So among actual engines (postgres, sqlite, mysql, the only values sqlglot_dialect_for_url returns), '#' is a comment only on MySQL. The one other path is dialect=None, where '#' also counts as a comment. The docstring at readonly.py:113-114 says this is deliberate, to count every engine's syntax, and None names no engine. The test comment is therefore accurate about engines, though its wording 'only in MySQL' omits the None union case. That omission is a minor imprecision, not a falsehood about any engine.
